title: The Hero War Pigeons of World War II
hook: Flown across enemy flak to deliver secret microfilm.

scenes.text: During World War II, when radio silence was vital to avoid detection, the British military deployed over 250,000 homing pigeons.
scenes.imagePrompt: Military mobile pigeon loft truck parked behind sandbagged hedgerow in countryside with open wicker release baskets. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: During World War II, when radio silence was vital to avoid detection, the British military deployed over 250,000 homing pigeons.

scenes.text: RAF bomber crews carried pigeons in sealed floating watertight canisters in case their aircraft was shot down into the freezing sea.
scenes.imagePrompt: Wicker aircraft basket lined with straw and blue canvas straps beside an aircraft instrument panel. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: RAF bomber crews carried pigeons in sealed floating watertight canisters in case their aircraft was shot down into the freezing sea.

scenes.text: Downed airmen scribbled their ocean coordinates onto thin tissue paper, rolled it into an aluminum leg capsule, and released the bird.
scenes.imagePrompt: Close-up of a tiny silver aluminum message tube with screw cap resting on damp flight chart paper. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Downed airmen scribbled their ocean coordinates onto thin tissue paper, rolled it into an aluminum leg capsule, and released the bird.

scenes.text: Birds like 'Winkie' flew over one hundred miles across stormy seas through gunfire and hawk attacks to alert rescue sea launches.

scenes.text: Thirty-two pigeons were awarded the Dickin Medal—the animal equivalent of the Victoria Cross—for gallantry under enemy fire.
